title: Global functions
lede: JavaScript's language-level globals — numeric parsing, type coercion, URI/base64 codecs, and deep cloning — compiled to plain C-stdlib calls with no runtime engine. globalThis.X works as an alias for the bare ambient global X (member access to known globals only — there's no dynamic global object). Dynamic eval is out of scope — it needs the (unstarted) embedded engine, though a compile-time-constant eval("<expression>") does route through this compiler's own parser. Malformed input is rejected where JS rejects it — decodeURI/decodeURIComponent throw URIError and atob enforces forgiving-base64 with QuotaExceededError.

entries.name: isNaN(x)
entries.description: Reports whether a number is NaN. Compiled as an unordered float comparison, so it agrees with NaN's defining self-inequality.

entries.name: isFinite(x)
entries.description: Reports whether a number is neither NaN nor an infinity.

returns.desc: true if x is a finite number.

entries.name: String(x)
entries.description: Coerces a value to its string form. Routes through the template-literal renderer; an any input dispatches on its runtime tag.
differences: `String()` with no argument is `""`, not real JS's `"undefined"` (a genuinely absent value doesn't arise in typed code).

entries.name: Number(x)
entries.description: Coerces a value to a number using JS ToNumber semantics: a whole-string parse ("12px" is NaN, unlike parseFloat), ""/whitespace is 0, "0x10" is 16, boolean is 0/1, null is 0; a numeric input passes through unchanged (an exact i64 stays i64). Only the exact word "Infinity" (optionally signed) is Infinity — C's "inf"/case variants are NaN, matching real JS.
entries.snippet:
const n = Number(s);
if (Number.isNaN(n)) { throw new TypeError("not a number: " + s); }

entries.name: Boolean(x)
entries.description: Coerces a value to a boolean using the shared truthiness rules (NaN, "", and 0 are falsy).

entries.name: parseInt(s, radix?)
entries.description: Parses a leading integer out of a string, stopping at the first non-digit. A no-digits input returns a real NaN (endptr-checked, double result). With radix omitted, auto-detects base 16 for a "0x"/"0X" prefix (parseInt("0xFF") is 255) and base 10 otherwise — no octal auto-detect, so "077" is 77.

params.name: radix
params.desc: Base 2–36; defaults to 10, or 16 for a "0x" prefix.

entries.snippet:
console.log(parseInt('3abc'))      // 3   (stops at first non-digit)
console.log(parseInt('0xFF'))      // 255 (auto-detected hex)
console.log(parseInt('FF', 16))    // 255

entries.name: parseFloat(s)
entries.description: Parses a leading floating-point number out of a string. A "0x" hex prefix reads only its leading 0 → 0 (real parseFloat, unlike Number("0x10") → 16). A no-conversion input returns a real NaN; only the exact word "Infinity" parses to Infinity ("inf" is NaN).

entries.name: NaN (global constant)
entries.description: The bare NaN global (same value as Number.NaN), usable without the Number. prefix. NaN != x and !== x comparisons are correct — compiled as unordered fcmp une, so NaN !== NaN is true as in JS.
entries.snippet:
const nan: float64 = NaN
console.log(nan !== nan)           // true  (the defining property of NaN)
differences: `let NaN = 99;` is a reserved-name collision under the default `-compat=strict`; `-compat=js` allows the shadow real JS permits.

entries.name: Infinity (global constant)
entries.description: The bare Infinity global (same value as Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY), usable without the Number. prefix; -Infinity is the negative pole.
differences: Same shadowing caveat as `NaN` above — needs `-compat=js`, not unconditional.

entries.name: undefined (global constant)
entries.description: The undefined global, as a literal value.

entries.name: globalThis
entries.description: globalThis.X desugars to the bare ambient global X, so the standard portable alias works for member access — including nested and call forms like globalThis.JSON.stringify(...), globalThis.Math.max(...), and globalThis.setTimeout(...). There is no dynamic global object: only known globals resolve (an unknown globalThis.foo is a compile error), and a bare globalThis as a value, computed access (globalThis["x"]), and assigning a new global are unsupported.
caveats: Only member access to known globals resolves — no dynamic global record
Bare globalThis as a value, globalThis["x"], and globalThis.x = … are unsupported

entries.name: encodeURI(s)
entries.description: Percent-encodes a whole URI, leaving the unreserved and reserved (;/?:@&=+$,#) character sets unescaped so the URI's own structure survives.
entries.snippet:
console.log(encodeURI("http://example.com/path?a=1&b=2 space"))
// http://example.com/path?a=1&b=2%20space (only the space got escaped)

entries.name: decodeURI(s)
entries.description: Decodes a whole URI; a malformed escape throws a URIError as in JS. Does not decode a %XX escape representing a reserved character (leaves it as literal %XX text) — the one real behavioral difference from decodeURIComponent.
entries.snippet:
console.log(decodeURI("http://example.com/path%3Fa=1&b=2%20space"))
// http://example.com/path%3Fa=1&b=2 space (%3F stays literal — it's '?', reserved)

entries.name: encodeURIComponent(s)
entries.description: Percent-encodes a single query-string value or path segment, leaving only the unreserved set (letters, digits, -_.!~*'()) unescaped.

entries.name: decodeURIComponent(s)
entries.description: Decodes a query-string value or path segment, decoding every valid %XX escape unconditionally.

entries.name: atob(s)
entries.description: Base64 decode implementing WHATWG forgiving-base64: ASCII whitespace is stripped, a missing-padding trailing group still decodes, a remaining length ≡ 1 (mod 4) throws InvalidCharacterError, and an interior or excess `=` (accepted only as trailing padding) throws too. Operates byte-for-byte on the input string (this compiler's strings are already plain byte sequences — no separate "binary string" type needed).

returns.desc: The decoded bytes as a string.

entries.snippet:
console.log(atob("aGVsbG8="))                   // hello
console.log(atob(btoa("round trip 123!@#")))    // round trip 123!@#

entries.name: btoa(s)
entries.description: Base64 encode, =-padded (RFC 4045).

entries.name: structuredClone(obj)
entries.description: A real recursive deep copy, dispatched entirely on the argument's static type: arrays (incl. nested and TypedArrays), plain objects, and Maps/Sets recurse into freshly allocated storage, cloning every entry deeply; scalars pass through as value types. The result is fully independent of the original.
differences: `EventEmitter`/`URL`/`URLSearchParams`/functions/class instances/`Promise`/`any`/`unknown` are rejected at compile time rather than silently aliased (`URL` matches Node, which throws `DataCloneError`); a `Map`/`Set` with an array/Map/Set key or value element type is also rejected (only scalar/string/object elements clone). A plain `ArrayBuffer` is byte-copied, a `SharedArrayBuffer` passes by reference, and an `Error` (or subtype) copies its kind/message/name.

entries.name: queueMicrotask(fn)
entries.description: A FIFO of callback closures, run after the current synchronous script and before timers.

params.name: fn
params.desc: Callback to run as a microtask.

differences: Drained at the reachable checkpoints (end of the top-level script, each scheduler step); a program with neither timers nor async tasks drains once at exit.

entries.name: gc()
entries.description: The Node --expose-gc global.gc() idiom; added to make weak-reference reclamation deterministically observable.
differences: A no-op under `-mm=manual` (the default) — nothing is ever collected; only meaningful under `-mm=gc`, where it forces a full Boehm collection.

entries.name: eval(s)
entries.description: General/dynamic eval is unimplemented (it needs the opt-in embedded engine, not started). A narrow static subset does work: a compile-time-constant eval("<expression>") is compiled in place through this compiler's own parser and codegen, no engine. A dynamic string, a statement/declaration, or a reference to a top-level binding is a clean compile error, never a runtime throw.

params.name: s
params.desc: A compile-time-constant expression string (static subset only).
